narrative: A mid level disturbance associated with a confluent upper level trough lead to strong mid level frontogenesis that developed a band of snow to the north of developing low pressure moving offshore. Southwestern portions of the area were on the northern edge of a narrow band of heavy snow that resulted in some southwestern zones reaching warning criteria.  Amounts were considerably less to the north.

evidence.event_narrative: A narrow band of heavy snow got into Richmond County (Staten Island) with the highest amounts over the southern half of the zone. A Cocorahs observer reported 7.8 inches at 1 N Tottenville. The public reported 10.0 inches at 1 WSW Tottenville, 9.5 inches at 1 SE Huguenot, 9.1 inches at 1 SSW Huguenot, 8.6 inches at 1 E New Dorp, 7.8 inches at 1 N Tottenville, and 6.8 inches at Westerleigh.  Further north in the zone only 3.5 inches was reported at 1 WNW Tompkinsville which corresponded well to radar and the band orientation.

A band of heavy snow got into most of Brooklyn, with perhaps far northern parts of the zone averaging below warning criteria with less reports further north and based on radar analysis and location of the stronger radar reflectivity. However most of the zone reported with warning criteria snowfall. Snowfall reports from Broadcast Media included 7.3 inches at Midwood. A trained spotter reported 8.0 inches at Sheepshead Bay and 5.2 inches at 2 WNW Crown Heights. Public reports around Bay Ridge varied from around 5 to 7.6 inches, and 6.5 inches in Williamsburg. The lowest report was from 2 W Crown Heights at 4.7 inches. Thus amounts of those reported averaged more than warning criteria and more than half the zone spatially reached warning criteria.

The far northern edge of a band of moderate to heavy snow stationed itself just south of Manhattan, although radar reflectivity returns indicate that the band scraped far southern Manhattan although reports from far Southern Manhattan did not come in. There were 5 and 6 inch reports just to the ESE over Kings (Brooklyn) and over Hudson County in NE NJ. The NWS Official Observation for the NWS indicated 2.0 inches in Central Park, and 3.2 inches at 1 SE Greenwich Village (Madison Park) via an NWS Employee / Contractor.

Reports of around 2 inches came in for the Bronx with the band of heavy snow going just to the south. A cocorahs report of 2.0 inches came in at 1 NE Riverdale and a public report of 2.1 inches at 1 ENE East Tremont.

A band of heavy snow got into the far southern portion of Queens County. However, most of the zone fell short of warning criteria from a coverage perspective. This is based on reports and radar reflectivity returns. The highest amount reported was from the general public in Breezy Point with 8.9 inches and this matched up with radar returns as Breezy Point sticks out as the most southern point. Broadcast media at 4 ENE Breezy Point (Coney Island vicinity) reported 8.0 inches. Also, the NWS Official Observation at JFK reported 6.2 inches. However, this was only a very narrow stripe of warning level snow across far southern portions of the zone.  A trained spotter reported 3.3 inches a 2 S Elmhurst, the public reported 3.0 inches at 1WNW Elmhurs, and the Official NWS Observation at LGA reported 3.3 inches of snow.  There was also a 3.3 inch amount reported just to the west across Northern Brooklyn.

A band of heavy to moderate snow moved just to the immediate south of Northern Queens. Amounts ranged around 3 inches across the zone. The Official NWS Observation from LGA reported 3.3 inches. A public report at 1 WNW Elmhurst came in at 3.0 inches.  Also a report came in from Woodside at 3.0 inches.
